raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence", "note": "The shutdown often masks a quiet fear of not being capable enough to figure out what comes next — avoidance dressed up as indifference." },
  "read": "At almost 18, being asked about college or life plans is essentially being asked 'who are you going to be?' before they know the answer. That question hits status hard — if they guess wrong out loud, in front of you, they look lost or incompetent. Shutting down is self-protection, not laziness or defiance.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Push harder every time they go quiet — keep asking, keep listing reasons, keep reminding them deadlines exist — which makes the conversation feel like a cross-examination and guarantees the wall goes higher." },
  "mentorMove": "Back the conversation away from the destination and toward the person standing in front of you. You're not trying to get answers tonight; you're trying to make it safe enough that they eventually want to think out loud with you instead of hiding from you.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The expectation that they engage with what comes next is non-negotiable — some plan, some direction, some active thinking is required before graduation, full stop.",
    "Silence and shutdown are not an acceptable long-term response; you will keep coming back to this, gently, until you're having a real conversation."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "The timeline and format of that conversation is totally up to them — a walk, a drive, a late-night kitchen talk, whatever lowers the stakes.",
    "College is one path, not the only path; what you're holding them to is intentional thinking about the future, not a specific answer.",
    "They don't have to have it figured out — they just have to be willing to figure it out with you."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to try something different. Every time I bring up next year you go quiet, and I've realized I've probably been making it feel like a quiz you could fail. That's on me. I'm not here for the right answer tonight." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I just ask — when you think about the year after graduation, what's the feeling? Not the plan, just the feeling. Because I remember being right where you are, and it was honestly more overwhelming than I ever admitted to anyone." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "What if we just talked about what sounds interesting to you — not what you should do, not what I think makes sense, just what pulls at you even a little? We can look stupid ideas in the eye together and figure out which ones are actually worth something." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm going to keep bringing this up, not to pressure you but because I think you have a lot more clarity in you than you're giving yourself credit for right now. I have genuinely high expectations for your life, and I hold them because I know you can meet them — I just want us to work on this together before the calendar makes the decision for us." }
  ],
  "longGame": "The goal isn't a college list by Thursday — it's building a pattern where they bring you the hard questions instead of hiding them. Every time you stay calm when they shut down, you make the next conversation more likely. Stay curious longer than feels comfortable, and the real thinking will eventually come out."
}
situation: My almost-18-year-old shuts down every time college or life after graduation comes up.
